title: Sunshine Against Stress: A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Vitamin D Supplementation for Allostatic Load in a Conflict-Affected Population of Azad Jammu & Kashmir
content: Background: Vitamin D deficiency is a persistent global micronutrient deficiency linked to elevated allostatic load, the cumulative physiological wear and tear from chronic stress. Vitamin D may buffer this burden via anti-inflammatory, metabolic, and HPA-axis pathways. Objective: To evaluate the effect of Vitamin D supplementation on allostatic load in a conflict-exposed population. Methods: In this double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06101589), 127 adults in Haveli District, Azad Jammu and Kashmir were randomised to vitamin D (three 200,000 IU doses, 4-week intervals) or olive-oil placebo; 125 (65 vitamin D, 60 placebo) completed baseline and follow-up assessment. Results: Vitamin D significantly improved LDL, total and HDL cholesterol, BMI, waist-hip ratio, and perceived stress (PSS-10) versus placebo (all FDR-adjusted p<0.01), with no treatment-specific effect on blood pressure or HbA1c. The composite Allostatic Load score declined significantly more with vitamin D (adjusted difference −0.54, p<0.001; group-by-time interaction p<0.001). Mediation analysis showed that reduced perceived stress explained approximately 46% of this effect (indirect effect = −0.28, 95% CI = −0.48 to −0.11). Conclusion: Vitamin D supplementation reduced allostatic load relative to placebo through direct metabolic and stress-mediated pathways, supporting its potential as a low-cost intervention in conflict-affected, high-stress settings.
